##### Summary
Fixes #8421
Fixes #8384
##### Component Name
database/dbengine
##### Test Plan
Test scenario with dbengine page cache size smaller than the amount of metrics being generated by collectors.

Test scenario with disks being slower than metric data generation throughput for potential regression detection.

have covered, and recreate them if necessary. If sufficient tests are covered
by our CI, then state which tests cover the change.
-->

##### Additional Information
Fix flushing error threshold to account for inactive producers of dbengine instance.

Hi,

I am having the same issue in v1.20 with the following setup : 

- 10 headless, memory = none collectors, streaming to a central colector

>v1.20.0

>dbengine

comments: Ok, I think the problem is with the interaction of the statsd native collector with memory mode `dbengine`, and the fact that the batching can create an unpredictably large number of outstanding pages. By calling the collector every 2 hours for instance it's possible that the corresponding `dbengine` instance runs out of free pages.
@jbfuzier can you test #8425 ?

Thanks, should I update the slave, the central collector or both ?
Statsd metrics are collected by the slave and streamed to the central collector.
Also is there an automated build somewhere or should I build this branch myself ?

It hasn't been merged to master yet, so you have to build it yourself, you can run `./netdata-installer.sh`. For example:
```
./netdata-installer.sh --install /opt
```
Installs netdata under `/opt/netdata`. For more details see the [documentation](https://docs.netdata.cloud/packaging/installer/methods/kickstart/#optional-parameters-to-alter-your-installation).

You should update whatever agent has the problem with dbengine, which I believe would be the central collector in this case.

```
git clone http://github.com/mfundul/netdata.git --depth=100 -b fix-flushing-errors
./netdata-installer.sh --disable-telemetry --disable-backend-mongodb --disable-backend-kinesis --disable-https --disable-cloud --disable-plugin-freeipmi --install /opt
```

Done, I hope I built the right one it says v1.20.0-180-nightly.

That doesn't sound right, but it's probably just your dashboard caching this information. You can run `netdata -V` and see what's the real version. It should be something like `v1.20.0-188-gcf618e19`

root@grafana:~/netdata# /opt/netdata/bin/netdata -V
netdata v1.20.0-180-nightly
I believe you should do a `git checkout fix-flushing-errors` in your cloned directory, and run a `git describe` that would give you the expected version. Then you should run the installer again.

Hmm, maybe `git describe` failing is the problem with the version number. In any case, you either have to run the installer as `root` user or with `sudo ./netdata-installer.sh`. You can compare your built binary with what's installed to make sure, e.g. `cmp /opt/netdata/usr/sbin/netdata ./netdata`.
